messages.author: 20a091f3d0e9ee8f
messages.subject: measurement invariance lanInspect
parts:
Dear all,

I was trying out a MI with HolzingerSwineford data and when I constrained the intercepts to be equal:

###MODEL 3 strong invariance model
model3 <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group="school",
 group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts"))
lavInspect(model3)
summary(model3,fit.measures=TRUE)

I saw in lavInspect, that only for of type of schools the intercepts of the latent variables are estimated and for the other group are fixed (see attached in red and blue):

Under 
$Pasteur$alpha
        intrcp
visual       0
textual      0
speed        0

but,
$`Grant-White`$alpha
        intrcp
visual      61
textual     62
speed       63

if they are meant to be equal, they should be listed at the beginning, together with the loadings and indicators intercepts:

Note: model contains equality constraints:

   lhs op rhs
1    1 ==  31
2    2 ==  32
3    3 ==  33
4    4 ==  34
5    5 ==  35
6    6 ==  36
7   22 ==  52
8   23 ==  53
9   24 ==  54
10  25 ==  55
11  26 ==  56
12  27 ==  57
13  28 ==  58
14  29 ==  59
15  30 ==  60

but as you see it is not the case...

Thank you!!
Michael.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: measurement invariance lanInspect
parts:
Michael--
Here, the keyword "intercepts" refers only to the intercepts of the observed variables, not the means / intercepts of the common factors. Imposing equality on the observed variable intercepts is a prerequisite for making across-group comparisons meaningful.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: measurement invariance lanInspect
parts:
Michael--
Even with equality of observed variable intercepts and loadings, factor means are not identified in absolute terms.default here is to fix factor means / intercepts to 0 in the first group. Then factor means / intercepts in other groups are identified relative to that 0. You could change which group's parameters are constrained to 0, you could change these constrained values to something other than 0, but you can't escape the arbitrary nature of factor means /. intercepts. That is part of the price of modeling using these imaginary variables. If you were modeling with composites instead of common factors, then these means would be specific functions of the observed variable means and the weights assigned to the observed variables.
